meaning_english: Viśvāmitra approached King Daśaratha and requested the young Rāma, who still wore side-locks, to remove obstacles to his sacrifice. Indeed, in the case of the brilliant, age is not a factor to be considered.

content_sanskrit: कृच्छ्रलब्धमपि लब्धवर्णभाक्यं दिदेश मुनये सलक्ष्मणम् । अप्यसुप्रणयिनां रघोः कुले न व्यहन्यत कदाचिदर्थिता ॥

meaning_english: The learned King Daśaratha gave Rāma, along with Lakṣmaṇa, to the sage, even though they were obtained with great difficulty. In the lineage of Raghu, a request is never refused, even if the seekers ask for life itself.

content_sanskrit: यावदादिशति पार्थिवास्तयोर्निर्गमाय पुरमार्गसंस्क्रियाम् । तावदाशु विदधे मरुत्सखैः सा सपुष्पजलवर्षिभिर्घनैः ॥

meaning_english: Just as the king was ordering the decoration of the city roads for the departure of the two princes, the clouds, friends of the wind, quickly performed that task by showering water and flowers.

content_sanskrit: तौ निदेशकरणोद्यतौ पितुर्धन्विनौ चरणयोर्निपेततुः । भूपतेरपि तयोः प्रवत्स्यतोर्नम्रयोरुपरि बाष्पबिन्दवः ॥

meaning_english: The two archers, ready to carry out their father's command, fell at his feet. As they bowed, about to depart, the king's teardrops also fell upon them.

content_sanskrit: तौ पितुर्नयनजेन वारिणा किंचिदुक्षितशिखण्डकावुभौ । धन्विनौ तमृषिमन्वगच्छतां पौरदृष्टिकृतमार्गतोरणौ ॥
padaccheda: तौ । पितुः । नयनजेन । वारिणा । किंचित् । उक्षितशिखण्डकौ । उभौ । धन्विनौ । तम् । ऋषिम् । अन्वगच्छताम् । पौरदृष्टिकृतमार्गतोरणौ

meaning_english: Both the archers, their locks slightly moistened by their father's tears, followed the sage. As they walked, the gazes of the citizens formed a continuous archway of welcome along their path.

content_sanskrit: लक्ष्मणानुचरमेव राघवं नेतुमैच्छदृषिरित्यसौ नृपः । आशिषं प्रयुयुजे न वाहिनीं सा हि रक्षणविधौ तयोः क्षमा ॥

meaning_english: Knowing the sage desired only Rāma followed by Lakṣmaṇa, the king offered only his blessings and not an army. Indeed, his blessing alone was sufficient for their protection.

content_sanskrit: मातृवर्गचरणस्पृशौ मुनेस्तौ प्रपद्य पदवीं महौजसः । रेचतुर्गतिवशात्प्रवर्तिनौ भास्करस्य मधुमाधवाविव ॥

meaning_english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, after touching the feet of their mothers, followed the path of the powerful sage Viśvāmitra. As they moved, they shone brilliantly like the two spring months, Madhu and Mādhava, following the course of the sun.

content_sanskrit: वीचिलोलभुजयोस्तयोर्गतं शैशवाञ्चपलमप्यशोभत । तोयदागम इवोद्ध्यभिद्ययोर्नामधेयसदृशं विचेष्टितम् ॥

meaning_english: The gait of the two brothers, though unsteady due to their childhood, looked beautiful with their arms swaying like waves. Their movement resembled the behavior of the rivers Uddhya and Abhidya during the monsoon, which act according to their names (breaking and rising).

content_sanskrit: तौ बलातिबलयोः प्रभावतो विद्ययोः पथि मुनिप्रदिष्टयोः । मम्लतुर्न मणिकुट्टिमोचितौ मातृपार्श्वपरिवर्तिनाविवि ॥

meaning_english: By the power of the two sciences, Balā and Atibalā, taught to them by the sage, the two brothers did not feel exhausted on the path. Though they were accustomed to jeweled floors and staying near their mothers, they remained as fresh as if they were still at home.

content_sanskrit: पूर्ववृत्तकथितैः पुराविदः सानुजः पितृसखस्य राघवः । उह्यमान इव वाहनोचितः पादचारमपि न व्यभावयत् ॥

meaning_english: Rāma, accompanied by his younger brother, did not even feel the fatigue of walking on foot, though he was accustomed to riding in vehicles. This was because he felt as if he were being carried along by the ancient legends narrated by the sage Viśvāmitra, his father's friend.

content_sanskrit: तौ सरांसि रसवद्भिरम्बुभिः कूजितैः श्रुतिसुखैः पतत्रिणः । वायवः सुरभिपुष्परेणुभिश्छायया च जलदाः सिषेविरे ॥

meaning_english: The lakes served the two brothers with sweet water, the birds with ear-pleasing warbling, the winds with fragrant flower pollen, and the clouds with their shade.

content_sanskrit: नाम्भसां कमलशोभिनां तथा शाखिनां च न परिश्रमच्छिदाम् । दर्शनेन लघुना यथा तयोः प्रीतिमापुरुभयोस्तपस्विनः ॥

meaning_english: The ascetics did not derive as much joy from the sight of lotus-adorned waters or fatigue-removing trees as they did from a brief glimpse of the two brothers.

content_sanskrit: स्थाणुदग्धवपुषस्तपोवनं प्राप्य दाशरथिरात्तकार्मुकः । विग्रहेण मदनस्य चारुणा सोऽभवत्प्रतिनिधिर्न कर्मणा ॥
padaccheda: स्थाणुदग्धवपुषः । तपोवनम् । प्राप्य । दाशरथिः । आत्तकार्मुकः । विग्रहेण । मदनस्य । चारुणा । सः । अभवत् । प्रतिनिधिः । न । कर्मणा

meaning_english: Upon reaching the penance grove where Śiva had burnt the body of Kāmadeva, Rāma, holding his bow, became a substitute for the God of Love through his beautiful physical form, though not through his actions.

content_sanskrit: तौ सुकेतुसुतया खिलीकृते कौशिकाद्विदितशापया पथि । निन्यतुः स्थलनिवेशिताटनी लीलयैव धनुषी अधिज्यताम् ॥

meaning_english: On the path made desolate by Tāḍakā (the daughter of Suketu), whose curse was explained to them by Viśvāmitra, the two brothers effortlessly strung their bows by resting the ends on the ground.

content_sanskrit: ज्यानिनादमथ गृह्णती तयोः प्रादुरास बहुलक्षपाछविः । ताडका चलकपालकुण्डला कालिकेव निबिडा बलाकिनी ॥

meaning_english: Then, responding to the sound of their bowstrings, Tāḍakā appeared. She had the complexion of a dark night and wore moving skulls as earrings, looking like a dense row of dark clouds accompanied by cranes.

content_sanskrit: तीव्रवेगधुतमार्गवृक्षया प्रेतचीवरवसा स्वनोग्रया । अभ्यभावि भरताग्रजस्तया वात्ययेव पितृकाननोत्थया ॥

anvaya: तीव्रवेगधुतमार्गवृक्षया स्वनोग्रया प्रेतचीवरवसा तया पितृकाननोत्थया वात्यया इव भरताग्रजः अभ्यभावि ।
meaning_english: Rāma was attacked by her, who roared fiercely and shook the trees along the path with her great speed. Wearing the clothes of the dead, she resembled a whirlwind rising from a cremation ground.

content_sanskrit: उद्यतैकभुजयष्टिमायतीं श्रोणिलम्बिपुरुषान्त्रमेखलाम् । तां विलोक्य वनितावधे घृणां पत्रिणा सह मुमोच राघवः ॥
padaccheda: उद्यतैकभुजयष्टिम् । आयतीम् । श्रोणिलम्बिपुरुषान्त्रमेखलाम् । ताम् । विलोक्य । वनितावधे । घृणाम् । पत्रिणा । सह । मुमोच । राघवः
anvaya: राघवः उद्यत-एक-भुज-यष्टिम् आयतीम् श्रोणि-लम्बि-पुरुष-अन्त्र-मेखलाम् ताम् विलोक्य, वनिता-वधे घृणाम् पत्रिणा सह मुमोच।
meaning_english: Seeing her (Tataka) approaching with one staff-like arm raised and wearing a girdle of human entrails dangling from her hips, Raghava (Rama) cast aside his hesitation about killing a woman and released his arrow along with his pity.

content_sanskrit: यञ्चकार विवरं शिलाघने ताडकोरसि स रामसायकः । अप्रविष्टविषयस्य रक्षसां द्वारतामगमदन्तकस्य तत् ॥
padaccheda: यत् । चकार । विवरम् । शिलाघने । ताडकोरसि । सः । रामसायकः । अप्रविष्टविषयस्य । रक्षसाम् । द्वारताम् । अगमत् । अन्तकस्य । तत्
anvaya: सः राम-सायकः शिला-घने ताडका-उरसि यत् विवरम् चकार, तत् रक्षसाम् अप्रविष्ट-विषयस्य अन्तकस्य द्वारताम् अगमत्।
meaning_english: The hole that Rama's arrow made in Tataka's stone-hard chest became a gateway to the demons for Yama, the god of death, whose domain they had not yet entered.

content_sanskrit: बाणभिन्नहृदया निपेतुषी सा स्वकाननभुवं न केवलाम् । विष्टपत्रयपराजयस्थिरां रावणश्रियमपि व्यकम्पयत् ॥
padaccheda: बाणभिन्नहृदया । निपेतुषी । सा । स्वकाननभुवम् । न । केवलाम् । विष्टपत्रयपराजयस्थिराम् । रावणश्रियम् । अपि । व्यकम्पयत्
anvaya: बाण-भिन्न-हृदया निपेतुषी सा केवलाम् स्व-कानन-भुवम् न (अकम्पयत्), (किन्तु) विष्टप-त्रय-पराजय-स्थिराम् रावण-श्रियम् अपि व्यकम्पयत्।
meaning_english: As she fell with her heart pierced by the arrow, she (Tataka) shook not only her own forest ground but also violently shook the sovereignty of Ravana, which had been made firm by his conquest of the three worlds.

content_sanskrit: राममन्मथशरेण ताडिता दुःसहेन हृदये निशाचरी । गन्धवद्रुधिरचन्दनोक्षिता जीवितेशवसतिं जगाम सा ॥

anvaya: दुःसहेन राम-मन्मथ-शरेण हृदये ताडिता, गन्धवत्-रुधिर-चन्दन-उक्षिता सा निशाचरी जीवितेश-वसतिम् जगाम।
meaning_english: Struck in the heart by Rama's unbearable arrow, that demoness, sprinkled with her fragrant blood as if it were sandalwood paste, departed to the abode of Yama, the lord of life.

content_sanskrit: नैर्ऋतघ्नमथ मन्त्रवन्मुनेः प्रापदस्त्रमवदानतोषितात् । ज्योतिरिन्धननिपाति भास्करात्सूर्यकान्त इव ताडकान्तकः ॥

meaning_english: Then, from the sage (Vishvamitra), who was pleased by his heroic deed, the slayer of Tataka (Rama) obtained demon-slaying weapons accompanied by mantras, just as a sunstone receives from the sun a fire-igniting light that falls upon fuel.

content_sanskrit: वामनाश्रमपदं ततः परं पावनं श्रुतमृषेरुपेयिवान् । उन्मनाः प्रथमजन्मचेष्टितान्यस्मरन्नपि बभूव राघवः ॥

meaning_english: Afterwards, Raghava reached the holy site of Vamana's hermitage, which he had heard of. There, though not consciously remembering the deeds of his previous birth (as Vamana), he became inexplicably agitated in mind.

content_sanskrit: आससाद मुनिरात्मनस्ततः शिष्यवर्गपरिकल्पितार्हणम् । बद्धपल्लवपुटाञ्जलिद्रुमं दर्शनोन्मुखमृगं तपोवनम् ॥
padaccheda: आससाद । मुनिः । आत्मनः । ततः । शिष्यवर्गपरिकल्पितार्हणम् । बद्धपल्लवपुटाञ्जलिद्रुमं । दर्शनोन्मुखमृगं । तपोवनम्
anvaya: ततः मुनिः आत्मनः शिष्य-वर्ग-परिकल्पित-अर्हणम्, बद्ध-पल्लव-पुट-अञ्जलि-द्रुमम्, दर्शन-उन्मुख-मृगम् तपः-वनम् आससाद।
meaning_english: Then the sage (Vishvamitra) reached his own penance grove, where worship had been prepared by his disciples, where the trees seemed to offer reverence with hands of folded leaf-buds, and where the deer were eager for his sight.

content_sanskrit: तत्र दीक्षितमृषिं ररक्षतुर्विघ्नतो दशरथात्मजौ शरैः । लोकमन्धतमसात्क्रमोदितौ रश्मिभिः शशिदिवाकराविव ॥
padaccheda: तत्र । दीक्षितम् । ऋषिं । ररक्षतुः । विघ्नतः । दशरथात्मजौ । शरैः । लोकम् । अन्धतमसात् । क्रमोदितौ । रश्मिभिः । शशिदिवाकरौ । इव
anvaya: तत्र दशरथ-आत्मजौ शरैः दीक्षितम् ऋषिम् विघ्नतः ररक्षतुः, इव क्रम-उदितौ शशि-दिवाकरौ रश्मिभिः लोकम् अन्धतमसात् (रक्षतः)।
meaning_english: There, the two sons of Dasharatha protected the consecrated sage from obstacles with their arrows, just as the moon and the sun, rising in succession, protect the world from blinding darkness with their rays.

content_sanskrit: वीक्ष्य वेदिमथ रक्तबिन्दुभिर्बन्धुजीवपृथुभिः प्रदूषिताम् । संभ्रमोऽभवदपोढकर्मणामृत्विजां च्युतविकङ्कतस्रुचाम् ॥
padaccheda: वीक्ष्य । वेदिम् । अथ । रक्तबिन्दुभिः । बन्धुजीवपृथुभिः । प्रदूषिताम् । संभ्रमः । अभवत् । अपोढकर्मणाम् । ऋत्विजाम् । च्युतविकङ्कतस्रुचाम्
anvaya: अथ बन्धुजीव-पृथुभिः रक्त-बिन्दुभिः प्रदूषिताम् वेदिम् वीक्ष्य, अपोढ-कर्मणाम् च्युत-विकङ्कत-स्रुचाम् ऋत्विजाम् संभ्रमः अभवत्।
meaning_english: Then, upon seeing the sacrificial altar defiled by drops of blood as large as Bandhujiva flowers, panic arose among the priests, who abandoned their ritual actions and dropped the ladles made of Vikankata wood from their hands.

content_sanskrit: उन्मुखः सपदि लक्ष्मणाग्रजो बाणमाश्रयमुखात्समुद्धरन् । रक्षसां बलमपश्यदम्बरे गृध्रपक्षपवनेरितध्वजम् ॥

meaning_english: Immediately, Lakshmana's elder brother (Rama), looking up while drawing an arrow from his quiver, saw the demonic force in the sky, their flags fluttering in the wind generated by the wings of vultures.

content_sanskrit: तत्र यावधिपती मखद्विषां तौ शरव्यमकरोत्स नेतरान् । किं महोरगविसर्पिविक्रमो राजिलेषु गरुडः प्रवर्तते? ॥

meaning_english: In that place, Rāma targeted only the two leaders of the demons and ignored the others. This is compared to Garuḍa, whose immense prowess is meant for great serpents; he does not deign to attack common water-snakes.

content_sanskrit: सोऽस्त्रमुग्रजवमस्त्रकोविदः संदधे धनुषि वायुदैवतम् । तेन शैलगुरुमप्यपातयत्पाण्डुपत्रमिव ताडकासुतम् ॥

meaning_english: Rāma, an expert in weaponry, fixed a swift Vāyavya missile on his bow. With it, he felled the son of Tāḍakā, who was as heavy as a mountain, making him fall as easily as a withered pale leaf.

content_sanskrit: यः सुबाहुरिति राक्षसोऽपरस्तत्र तत्र विससर्प मायया । तं क्षुरप्रशकलीकृतं कृती पत्रिणां व्यभजदाश्रमाद्वहिः ॥

meaning_english: The other demon, Subāhu, who was moving about using magic, was cut into pieces by the skillful Rāma with crescent-headed arrows and thrown outside the hermitage as food for birds.

content_sanskrit: इत्यपास्तमखविघ्नयोस्तयोः सांयुगीनमभिनन्द्य विक्रमम् । ऋत्विजः कुलपतेर्यथाक्रमं वाग्यतस्य निरवर्तयन्क्रियाः ॥

meaning_english: Having praised the martial prowess of the two princes who had removed all obstacles to the sacrifice, the priests of Sage Viśvāmitra completed the remaining sacrificial rites in the proper order while the Sage remained silent in his vow.

content_sanskrit: तौ प्रणामचलकाकपक्षकौ भ्रातराववभृथाक्लुतो मुनिः । आशिषामनुपदं समस्पृशद्दर्भपाटिततलेन पाणिना ॥

meaning_english: After the ritual bath, the Sage touched the two brothers, whose side-locks were swaying as they bowed, with his hand—its palm scarred by handling Darbha grass—immediately after pronouncing blessings upon them.

content_sanskrit: तं न्यमन्त्रयत संभृतक्रतुर्मैथिलः स मिथिलां व्रजन्वशी । राघवावपि निनाय बिभ्रतौ तद्धनुःश्रवणजं कुतूहलम् ॥
padaccheda: तम् । न्यमन्त्रयत । संभृतक्रतुः । मैथिलः । सः । मिथिलाम् । व्रजन् । वशी । राघवावपि । निनाय । बिभ्रतौ । तद्धनुःश्रवणजम् । कुतूहलम्
anvaya: संभृतक्रतुः वशी सः मैथिलः तम् न्यमन्त्रयत। मिथिलाम् व्रजन् राघवावपि तत्धनुःश्रवणजम् कुतूहलम् बिभ्रतौ निनाय।
meaning_english: King Janaka of Mithilā, who was preparing a sacrifice, invited Sage Viśvāmitra. The Sage, while proceeding to Mithilā, took the two Raghava princes along, as they were filled with curiosity after hearing about the famous bow of Śiva.

content_sanskrit: तैः शिवेषु वसतिर्गताध्वभिः सायमाश्रमतरुष्वगृह्यत । येषु दीर्घतपसः परिग्रहो वासवक्षणकलत्रतां ययौ ॥
padaccheda: तैः । शिवेषु । वसतिः । गताध्वभिः । सायम् । आश्रमतरुषु । अगृह्यत । येषु । दीर्घतपसः । परिग्रहः । वासवक्षणकलत्रताम् । ययौ
anvaya: गताध्वभिः तैः सायम् शिवेषु आश्रमतरुषु वसतिः अगृह्यत येषु दीर्घतपसः परिग्रहः वासवक्षणकलत्रताम् ययौ।
meaning_english: In the evening, the travelers took rest under the auspicious trees of the hermitage where the wife of the ascetic Gautama had once briefly become the consort of Indra.

content_sanskrit: प्रत्यपद्यत चिराय यत्पुनश्चारु गौतमवधूः शैलमयी । स्वं वपुः स किल किल्बिषच्छिदां रामपादरजसामनुग्रहः ॥
padaccheda: प्रत्यपद्यत । चिराय । यत् । पुनः । चारु । गौतमवधूः । शैलमयी । स्वम् । वपुः । सः । किल । किल्बिषच्छिदाम् । रामपादरजसाम् । अनुग्रहः

meaning_english: That the wife of Gautama, who had turned into stone, regained her own beautiful form after a long time was indeed the grace of the dust of Rāma's feet, which has the power to destroy all sins.

content_sanskrit: राघवान्वितमुपस्थितं मुनिं तं निशम्य जनको जनेश्वरः । अर्थकामसहितं सपर्यया देहबद्धमिव धर्ममभ्यगात् ॥

meaning_english: Hearing of the arrival of the Sage accompanied by the two Raghava princes, King Janaka went out to welcome him with offerings, as if he were welcoming embodied Dharma accompanied by Artha and Kāma.

meaning_english: As the residents of Videha drank in the sight of the two princes—who looked like the twin Punarvasu stars descended from heaven to earth—their minds considered even the momentary blinking of their eyes to be a loss or a deception.

content_sanskrit: यूपवत्यवसिते क्रियाविधौ कालवित्कुशिकवंशवर्धनः । राममिष्वसनदर्शनोत्सुकं मैथिलाय कथयांबभूव सः ॥

content_sanskrit: तस्य वीक्ष्य ललितं वपुः शिशोः पार्थिवः प्रथितवंशजन्मनः । स्वं विचिन्त्य च धनुर्दुरानमं पीडितो दुहितृशुल्कसंस्थया ॥

meaning_english: Seeing the delicate body of the young Rama, born of a renowned lineage, and considering his own bow which was difficult to bend, King Janaka felt distressed by the condition he had set for his daughter's marriage price.

content_sanskrit: अव्रवीञ्च भगवन्मतङ्गजैर्यद्बृहद्भिरपि कर्म दुष्करम् । तत्र नाहमनुमन्तुमुत्सहे मोघवृत्ति कलभस्य चेष्टितम् ॥

meaning_english: The King said, "O Venerable One! I do not dare to permit the futile effort of a young elephant calf in a task that is difficult even for full-grown elephants."

content_sanskrit: ह्रेपिता हि बहवो नरेश्वरास्तेन तात! धनुषा धनुर्भृतः । ज्यानिघातकठिनत्वचो भुजान्स्वान्विधूय धिगिति प्रतस्थिरे ॥

meaning_english: "O Sage! Many kings, skilled archers themselves, were humiliated by that bow. Shaking their arms, which were toughened by the impact of bowstrings, they departed crying 'Shame!' upon themselves."

content_sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच तमृषिर्निशम्यतां सारतोऽयमथवा गिरा कृतम् । चाप एव भवतो भविष्यति व्यक्तशक्तिरशनिर्गिराविव ॥

meaning_english: The sage replied to him, "Listen to his strength, or rather, enough with words. His power will be revealed on the bow itself, just as the power of a thunderbolt is revealed on a mountain."

content_sanskrit: एवमाप्तवचनात्स पौरुषं काकपक्षकधरेऽपि राघवे । श्रद्धधे त्रिदशगोपमात्रके दाहशक्तिमिव कृष्णवर्त्मनि ॥

meaning_english: Thus, due to the reliable words of the sage, the King believed in the prowess of Raghava, though he still wore the side-locks of childhood, just as one believes in the burning power of fire even when it is as small as an Indragopa insect.

content_sanskrit: व्यादिदेश गणशोऽथ पार्श्वगान्कार्मुकाभिहरणाय मैथिलः । तैजसस्य धनुषः प्रवृत्तये तोयदानिव सहस्रलोचनः ॥

meaning_english: Then the King of Mithila ordered his attendants in groups to bring the bow, just as Indra, the thousand-eyed god, commands the clouds to bring forth the brilliance of his thunderbolt.

content_sanskrit: तत्प्रसुप्तभुजगेन्द्रभीषणं वीक्ष्य दाशरथिराददे धनुः । विद्रुतक्रतुमृगानुसारिणं येन बाणमसृजद्वृषध्वजः ॥

meaning_english: Seeing that bow, which was as terrifying as a sleeping king of serpents, the son of Dasharatha took it up—the very bow with which Lord Shiva had once discharged an arrow at the sacrifice that had fled in the form of a deer.

content_sanskrit: आततज्यमकरोत्स संसदा विस्मयस्तिमितनेत्रमीक्षितः । शैलसारमपि नातियत्नतः पुष्पचापमिव पेशलं स्मरः ॥

meaning_english: Watched by the assembly with eyes motionless from wonder, Rama strung the bow, which was as hard as a mountain, without much effort, as if it were the delicate flower-bow of Kamadeva.

meaning_english: As the bow broke due to excessive pulling, it made a sound as harsh as a thunderbolt, as if announcing to the deeply resentful Parashurama that the warrior race had risen once again.

content_sanskrit: दृष्टसारमथ रुद्रकार्मुके वीर्यशुल्कमभिनन्द्य मैथिलः । राघवाय तनयामयोनिजां रूपिणीं श्रियमिव न्यवेदयत् ॥

meaning_english: After Rāma's strength was witnessed through the breaking of Śiva's bow, King Janaka, having congratulated him, offered his daughter Sītā—who was not born of a womb—to Rāma, as if she were the goddess Lakṣmī herself in embodied form.

content_sanskrit: मैथिलः सपदि सत्यसंगरो राघवाय तनयामयोनिजाम् । संनिधौ द्युतिमतस्तपोनिधेरग्निसाक्षिक इवातिसृष्टवान् ॥

meaning_english: The King of Mithilā, who was true to his word, immediately bestowed his daughter Sītā upon Rāma in the presence of the radiant sage Viśvāmitra, as if the sage himself were the sacred fire acting as a witness to the gift.

content_sanskrit: प्राहिणोञ्च महितं महाद्युतिः कोसलाधिपतये पुराधसम् । भृत्यभावि दुहितुः परिग्रहाद्दिश्यतां कुलमिदं निमेरिति ॥

meaning_english: The illustrious Janaka sent his honored priest to King Daśaratha with the message: 'By your acceptance of my daughter for your son, may this dynasty of Nimi be regarded as your servant.'

content_sanskrit: अन्वियेष सदृशीं स च स्नुषां प्राप चैनमनुकूलवाग्द्विजः । सद्य एव सुकृतां हि पच्यते कल्पवृक्षफलधर्मिकाङ्क्षितम् ॥

meaning_english: King Daśaratha was already seeking a suitable daughter-in-law when the messenger priest with favorable news reached him. For the virtuous, their desires ripen immediately, just like the fruit of the celestial wish-fulfilling tree.

content_sanskrit: तस्य कल्पितपुरस्क्रियाविधेः शुश्रुवान्वचनमग्रजन्मनः । उञ्चचाल बलभित्सखो वशी सैन्यरेणुमुषितार्कदीधितिः ॥

meaning_english: Having heard the Brahmin's words and honored him with hospitality, the self-controlled Daśaratha—a friend of Indra—set out for Mithilā. His vast army raised such a cloud of dust that it obscured the very rays of the sun.

content_sanskrit: आससाद मिथिलां स वेष्टयन्पीडितोपवनपादपां बलैः । प्रीतिरोधमसहिष्ट सा पुरी स्त्रीव कान्तपरिभोगमायतम् ॥

meaning_english: He reached Mithilā and surrounded it with his forces, which pressed against the trees of the city's gardens. The city endured this siege of affection just as a woman endures the long and intense embrace of her lover.

meaning_english: The two kings, Daśaratha and Janaka, who resembled Indra and Varuṇa and were steadfast in their duties, met and performed the marriage ceremonies for their daughters and sons with a grandeur that matched their immense power.

meaning_english: The four sons of King Daśaratha, having accepted their new brides, shone brilliantly. They appeared like the four successful means of royal policy—conciliation, gift-giving, sowing dissension, and force—personified for the king.

meaning_english: The princesses attained fulfillment through the princes, and the princes through them. That union of grooms and brides was as perfect and meaningful as the union of grammatical roots with their appropriate suffixes.

meaning_english: Having thus found joy and settled his four sons in their respective places, King Daśaratha, after bidding farewell to the King of Mithilā at the junction of three paths, returned to his own city.

meaning_english: Once, adverse winds blowing against them on the paths and shaking the flag-staffs like trees, violently afflicted his army, just as overflowing river currents distress the dry land.

meaning_english: King Daśaratha, knowing his duty, saw the portents like adverse winds and questioned his preceptor Vasiṣṭha regarding propitiatory rites. Vasiṣṭha lessened the King's anxiety by saying it would end well.

meaning_english: He bore the paternal heritage characterized by the sacred thread and a mighty bow from his mother's side, appearing like the sun accompanied by the moon, or a sandalwood tree inhabited by a snake.

meaning_english: By him, who stood by the command of his father whose soul was harsh with anger, pity was first conquered when he cut off the head of his trembling mother, and then the earth was conquered.

meaning_english: He shone, wearing a rosary of seeds on his right ear, as if he were performing a preliminary count on a pretext for the twenty-one times he had destroyed the Kṣatriyas.

meaning_english: King Daśaratha, the young son of Aja, became deeply despondent upon seeing Paraśurāma. He observed Paraśurāma consecrated by the vow of destroying the entire royal race, driven by the intense anger arising from his father's murder. Comparing his own vulnerable condition and the formidable presence of the sage-warrior, the king felt a profound sense of despair for his sons and his lineage.

meaning_english: The name 'Rāma' was shared by both Daśaratha's beloved son and his formidable enemy, Paraśurāma. This identical name produced conflicting emotions in the king, much like a jewel found on both a decorative necklace and a deadly serpent. To Daśaratha, the name was simultaneously dear to his heart because of his son and a source of great terror because of the fierce sage.

content_sanskrit: अर्ध्यमर्ध्यमिति वादिनं नृपं सोऽनवेक्ष्य मरताग्रजो यतः । क्षत्रकोपदहनार्चिषं ततः संदधे दृशमुदग्रतारकाम् ॥

anvaya: सः भरताग्रजः अर्घ्यम् अर्घ्यम् इति वादिनं नृपम् अनवेक्ष्य यतः ततः क्षत्रकोपदहनार्चिषम् उदग्रतारकां दृशं संदधे ।
meaning_english: Ignoring King Daśaratha, who was repeatedly offering him the traditional respectful 'arghya', Paraśurāma fixed his gaze intently upon Rāma. His eyes, with pupils raised in intensity, burned like the flames of his legendary wrath against the Kṣatriya race. He completely disregarded the king's hospitality, focusing his entire formidable attention on the young prince who shared his name.

content_sanskrit: तेन कार्मुकनिषक्तमुष्टिना राघवो विगतभीः पुरोगतः । अङ्गुलीविवरचारिणं शरं कुर्वता निजगदे युयुत्सुना ॥

meaning_english: Paraśurāma, eager for a challenge, stood with his fist firmly on his bow, twirling an arrow between his fingers. He then addressed Rāma, who stood fearlessly before him. The sage's posture and the casual yet menacing way he handled his weapon signaled his combative intent, yet the young Raghu prince remained undaunted in the face of the legendary warrior's scrutiny.

content_sanskrit: क्षत्रजातमपकारवैरि मे तन्निहत्य बहुशः शमं गतः । सुप्तसर्प इव दण्डघट्टनाद्रोषितोऽस्मि तव विक्रमश्रवात् ॥
padaccheda: क्षत्रजातम् । अपकारवैरि । मे । तद् । निहत्य । बहुशः । शमम् । गतः । अस्मि । सुप्तसर्प । इव । दण्डघट्टनात् । रोषितः । अस्मि । तव । विक्रमश्रवात्

meaning_english: Paraśurāma declared that after repeatedly destroying the Kṣatriya race—his enemies for the injury done to his father—he had finally attained peace. However, hearing of Rāma's extraordinary prowess had provoked him once more. He compared himself to a sleeping serpent that has been rudely awakened and enraged by the strike of a staff, indicating that Rāma's fame had disturbed his quietude and reignited his warrior spirit.

content_sanskrit: मैथिलस्य धनुरन्यपार्थिवैस्त्वं किलानमितपूर्वमक्षणोः । तन्निशम्य भवता समर्थये वीर्यश्रृङ्गमिव भग्नमात्मनः ॥
padaccheda: मैथिलस्य । धनुः । अन्यपार्थिवैः । अनमितपूर्वम् । अक्षणोः । किल । तत् । निशम्य । भवता । समर्थये । वीर्यश्रृङ्गम् । इव । भग्नम् । आत्मनः

meaning_english: Paraśurāma remarked that Rāma had reportedly broken the bow of the King of Mithilā, a feat no other king had ever managed. Upon hearing this news, Paraśurāma felt as though his own 'horn of prowess'—his unique reputation for strength—had been broken by Rāma. He viewed Rāma's success not just as a feat of strength, but as a direct challenge to his own unmatched status as a warrior.

content_sanskrit: अन्यदा जगति राम इत्ययं शब्द उञ्चरित एव मामगात् । व्रीडमावहति मे स संप्रति व्यास्तवृत्तिरुदयोन्मुखे त्वयि ॥
padaccheda: अन्यदा । जगति । राम । इति । अयम् । शब्दः । उच्चरितः । एव । माम् । अगात् । संप्रति । उदयोन्मुखे । त्वयि । सः । व्यास्तवृत्तिः । मे । व्रीडम् । आवहति
anvaya: अन्यदा जगति राम इति अयं शब्दः उच्चरितः एव माम् अगात् । संप्रति उदयोन्मुखे त्वयि सः व्यास्तवृत्तिः मे व्रीडम् आवहति ।
meaning_english: In the past, the name 'Rāma' uttered in the world referred only to Paraśurāma. However, now that the young Rāma is rising in fame, the name has a divided application, referring to both of them. Paraśurāma expressed that this shared identity brings him a sense of shame, as his once-unique name and the glory associated with it are now being shared with another.

content_sanskrit: बिभ्रतोऽस्त्रमचलेऽप्यकुण्ठितं द्वौ रिपू मम मतौ समागसौ । धेनुवत्सहरणाञ्च हैहयस्त्वं च कीर्तिमपहर्तुमुद्यतः ॥
padaccheda: बिभ्रतः । अस्त्रम् । अचले । अपि । अकुण्ठितम् । द्वौ । रिपू । मम । मतौ । समागसौ । धेनुवत्सहरणात् । हैहयः । त्वम् । च । कीर्तिम् । अपहर्तुम् । उद्यतः

meaning_english: Paraśurāma, whose weapons remain unblunted even against mountains, considers two enemies equally guilty of offending him. One is the Haihaya king, who stole his father's calf, and the other is Rāma, who is now striving to steal his fame. By equating the loss of his fame to the theft of his family's sacred property, Paraśurāma justifies his hostility toward the young prince.

content_sanskrit: क्षत्रियान्तकरणोऽपि विक्रमस्तेन मामवति नाजिते त्वयि । पावकस्य महिमा स गण्यते कक्षवज्ज्वलति सागरेऽपि यः ॥

meaning_english: Paraśurāma stated that his prowess, though famous for destroying the Kṣatriya race, does not satisfy him as long as Rāma remains unconquered. He explained that the true greatness of fire is recognized only when it can burn even in the middle of the ocean, just as it burns through dry grass. Similarly, his own power is only truly validated if it can overcome a formidable opponent like Rāma.

content_sanskrit: विद्धि चात्तबलमोजसा हरेरैश्वरं धनुरभाजि यत्त्वया । खातमूलमनिलो नदीरयैः पातयत्यपि मृदुस्तटद्रुमम् ॥
padaccheda: विद्धि । च । आत्तबलम् । ओजसा । हरेः । ऐश्वरम् । धनुः । यत् । त्वया । अभाजि । खातमूलम् । अनिलः । नदीरयैः । पातयति । अपि । मृदुः । तटद्रुमम्

meaning_english: Paraśurāma told Rāma that the bow of Śiva he broke had already been weakened by the power of Viṣṇu. He used an analogy to diminish Rāma's feat: even a gentle breeze can topple a massive tree on a riverbank if its roots have already been undermined by the river's current. Thus, he suggested that Rāma's breaking of the bow was not a true testament to his strength, but rather the result of the weapon's prior depletion.

content_sanskrit: तन्मदीयमिदमायुधं ज्यया संगमय्य सशरं विकृष्यताम् । तिष्ठतु प्रधनमेवमप्यहं तुल्यबाहुतरसा जितस्त्वया ॥

meaning_english: Parashurama tells Rama, "Therefore, string this bow of mine, fit an arrow, and draw it. Let the battle be. Even so, I am already conquered by you, by the strength of your equally powerful arms."

content_sanskrit: कातरोऽसि यदि वाद्गतार्चिषा तर्जितः परशुधारया मम । ज्यानिघातकठिनाङ्गुलिर्वृथा बध्यतामभयययाचनाञ्जलिः ॥

meaning_english: Parashurama continues, "Or if you are a coward, threatened by the blazing edge of my axe, then let your cupped hands, whose fingers are hardened by striking the bowstring, be folded in vain to beg for safety."

content_sanskrit: एवमुक्तवति भीमदर्शने भार्गवे स्मितविकम्पिताधरः । तद्धनुर्ग्रहणमेव राघवः प्रत्यपद्यत समर्थमुत्तरम् ॥

meaning_english: When the fearsome-looking Bhargava (Parashurama) had spoken thus, Raghava (Rama), his lower lip quivering with a smile, considered the very act of taking that bow as the fitting reply.

meaning_english: Reunited with the bow from his previous incarnation (as Vishnu), he (Rama) appeared extremely graceful and effortless. A new cloud is beautiful even by itself; what then when it is adorned with a rainbow?

content_sanskrit: तेन भूमिनिहितैककोटि तत्कार्मुकं च बलिनाधिरोपितम् । निष्प्रभश्च रिपुरास भूभृतां धूमशेष इव धूमकेतनः ॥

meaning_english: The powerful Rama strung that bow, placing one end on the ground. And the enemy of kings (Parashurama) became devoid of lustre, like a fire or comet that is reduced to mere smoke.

content_sanskrit: तावुभावपि परस्परस्थितौ वर्धमानपरिहीनतेजसौ । पश्यति स्म जनता दिनात्यये पार्वणौ शशिदिवाकराविव ॥

meaning_english: The people saw those two standing opposite each other, one with waxing and the other with waning splendour, like the moon and the sun seen together at dusk during a specific lunar phase.

content_sanskrit: तं कृपामृदुरवेक्ष्य भार्गवं राघवः स्खलितवीर्यमात्मनि । स्वं च संहितममोघमाशुगं व्याजहार हरसूनुसंनिभः ॥

meaning_english: Raghava, who resembled Kartikeya, looked with compassion upon Bhargava, whose power had faltered within him. Then, referring to his own unfailing arrow fitted on the bow, he spoke.

content_sanskrit: न प्रहर्तुमलमस्मि निर्दयं विप्र इत्यभिभवत्यपि त्वयि । शंस किं गतिमनेन पत्रिणा हन्मि लोकमुत ते मखार्जितम् ॥

meaning_english: Rama said, "Even though you assail me, I am not able to strike you mercilessly, because you are a Brahmin. Tell me, with this arrow, shall I destroy your power of movement, or the heavenly realms you have earned through sacrifices?"

content_sanskrit: प्रत्युवाच तमृषिर्न तत्त्वतस्त्वां न वेद्मि पुरुषं पुरातनम् । गां गतस्य तव धाम वैष्णवं कोपितो ह्यसि मया दिदृक्षुणा ॥
padaccheda: प्रति । उवाच । तम् । ऋषिः । न । तत्त्वतः । त्वाम् । न । वेद्मि । पुरुषम् । पुरातनम् । गाम् । गतस्य । तव । धाम । वैष्णवम् । कोपितः । हि । असि । मया । दिदृक्षुणा
anvaya: ऋषिः तम् प्रति उवाच - (अहम्) त्वाम् पुरातनम् पुरुषम् तत्त्वतः न वेद्मि (इति) न । हि दिदृक्षुणा मया गाम् गतस्य तव वैष्णवम् धाम (द्रष्टुम्) त्वम् कोपितः असि ।
meaning_english: The sage replied: "It is not that I do not know you in truth to be the ancient Purusha (Vishnu). Indeed, you were provoked by me, who, desiring to see your divine Vaishnava power now that you have come to earth, angered you."

content_sanskrit: भस्मसात्कृतवतः पितृद्विषः पात्रसाञ्च वसुधां ससागराम् । आहितो जयविपर्ययोऽपि मे श्लाध्य एव परमेष्ठिना त्वया ॥
padaccheda: भस्मसात्कृतवतः । पितृद्विषः । पात्रसात् । च । वसुधाम् । ससागराम् । आहितः । जयविपर्ययः । अपि । मे । श्लाध्यः । एव । परमेष्ठिना । त्वया
anvaya: पितृद्विषः भस्मसात् कृतवतः ससागराम् वसुधाम् च पात्रसात् (कृतवतः) मे, परमेष्ठिना त्वया आहितः जयविपर्ययः अपि श्लाध्यः एव ।
meaning_english: Parashurama said: "For me, who reduced my father's enemies to ashes and gave away the entire earth with its oceans to a worthy recipient, even this defeat inflicted by you, the Supreme Lord, is indeed praiseworthy."

content_sanskrit: तद्गतिं मतिमतां वरेप्सितां पुण्यतीर्थगमनाय रक्ष मे । पीडयिष्यति न मां खिलीकृता स्वर्गपद्धतिरभोगलोलुपम् ॥
padaccheda: तत् । गतिम् । मतिमताम् । वर । ईप्सिताम् । पुण्यतीर्थगमनाय । रक्ष । मे । पीडयिष्यति । न । माम् । खिलीकृता । स्वर्गपद्धतिः । अभोगलोलुपम्
anvaya: तत्, मतिमताम् वर, मे ईप्सिताम् गतिम् पुण्यतीर्थगमनाय रक्ष । खिलीकृता स्वर्गपद्धतिः अभोगलोलुपम् माम् न पीडयिष्यति ।
meaning_english: "Therefore, O best among the wise, spare my power of movement, which I desire for pilgrimages to holy sites. The path to heaven being blocked will not pain me, as I am not greedy for its enjoyments."

content_sanskrit: प्रत्यपद्यत तथेति राघवः प्राङ्मुखश्च विससर्ज सायकम् । भार्गवस्य सुकृतोऽपि सोऽभवत्स्वर्गमार्गपरिघो दुरत्ययः ॥
padaccheda: प्रत्यपद्यत । तथा । इति । राघवः । प्राङ्मुखः । च । विससर्ज । सायकम् । भार्गवस्य । सुकृतः । अपि । सः । अभवत् । स्वर्गमार्गपरिघः । दुरत्ययः
anvaya: राघवः 'तथा' इति प्रति अपद्यत, प्राङ्मुखः च सायकम् विससर्ज । सः (सायकः) भार्गवस्य सुकृतस्य अपि दुरत्ययः स्वर्गमार्गपरिघः अभवत् ।
meaning_english: Raghava agreed, saying "So be it," and facing east, released the arrow. That arrow became an insurmountable bar to the heavenly worlds earned by Bhargava's merit.

content_sanskrit: राघवोऽपि चरणौ तपोनिधेः क्षम्यतामिति वदन्समस्पृशत् । निर्जितेषु तरसा तरस्विनां शत्रुषु प्रणतिरेव कीर्तये ॥
padaccheda: राघवः । अपि । चरणौ । तपोनिधेः । क्षम्यताम् । इति । वदन् । समस्पृशत् । निर्जितेषु । तरसा । तरस्विनाम् । शत्रुषु । प्रणतिः । एव । कीर्तये
anvaya: राघवः अपि 'क्षम्यताम्' इति वदन् तपोनिधेः चरणौ समस्पृशत् । तरस्विनाम् तरसा निर्जितेषु शत्रुषु प्रणतिः एव कीर्तये (भवति) ।
meaning_english: Raghava, saying "Forgive me," touched the feet of the sage, that treasure of penance. For the powerful, showing respect to enemies conquered by force is itself a source of glory.

content_sanskrit: राजसत्वमवधूय मातृकं पित्र्यमस्मि गमितः शमं यदा । नन्वनिन्दितफलो मम त्वया निग्रहोऽप्ययमनुग्रहीकृतः ॥
padaccheda: राजसत्वम् । अवधूय । मातृकम् । पित्र्यम् । अस्मि । गमितः । शमम् । यदा । ननु । अनिन्दितफलः । मम । त्वया । निग्रहः । अपि । अयम् । अनुग्रहीकृतः
anvaya: यदा मातृकम् राजसत्वम् अवधूय पित्र्यम् शमम् गमितः अस्मि, ननु त्वया मम अयम् निग्रहः अपि अनिन्दितफलः अनुग्रहीकृतः ।
meaning_english: Parashurama said: "Since I have been made to shake off the quality of Rajas inherited from my mother and attain the tranquility inherited from my father, indeed, even this subjugation of me by you has been turned into a favor with a praiseworthy result."

content_sanskrit: साधयाम्यहमविघ्नमस्तु ते देवकार्यमुपपादयिष्यतः । ऊचिवानिति वचः सलक्ष्मणं लक्ष्मणाग्रजमृषिस्तिरोदधे ॥
padaccheda: साधयामि । अहम् । अविघ्नम् । अस्तु । ते । देवकार्यम् । उपपादयिष्यतः । ऊचिवान् । इति । वचः । सलक्ष्मणम् । लक्ष्मणाग्रजम् । ऋषिः । तिरोदधे
anvaya: अहम् साधयामि । देवकार्यम् उपपादयिष्यतः ते अविघ्नम् अस्तु । ऋषिः सलक्ष्मणम् लक्ष्मणाग्रजम् इति वचः ऊचिवान् तिरोदधे ।
meaning_english: "I shall now depart. May there be no obstacles for you as you accomplish the work of the gods." Having said these words to Rama, who was with Lakshmana, the sage disappeared.

content_sanskrit: तस्मिन्गते विजयिनं परिरभ्य रामं स्नेहादमन्यत पिता पुनरेव जातम् । तस्याभवत्क्षणशुचः परितोषलाभः कक्षाग्निलङ्घिततरोरिव वृष्टिपातः ॥
padaccheda: तस्मिन् । गते । विजयिनम् । परिरभ्य । रामम् । स्नेहात् । अमन्यत । पिता । पुनः । एव । जातम् । तस्य । अभवत् । क्षणशुचः । परितोषलाभः । कक्षाग्निलङ्घिततरोः । इव । वृष्टिपातः
anvaya: तस्मिन् गते (सति), पिता विजयिनम् रामम् परिरभ्य स्नेहात् पुनः एव जातम् अमन्यत । क्षणशुचः तस्य परितोषलाभः कक्षाग्निलङ्घिततरोः वृष्टिपातः इव अभवत् ।
meaning_english: When Parashurama had gone, his father Dasharatha embraced the victorious Rama and, out of affection, considered him born anew. For Dasharatha, whose grief had been momentary, the attainment of joy was like a rainfall upon a tree scorched by a forest fire.

content_sanskrit: अथ पथि गमयित्वा क्लृप्तरम्योपकार्ये कतिचिदवनिपालः शर्वरीः शर्वकल्पः । पुरमविशदयोध्यां मैथिलीदर्शनीनां कुवलयितगवाक्षां लोचनैरङ्गनानाम् ॥
padaccheda: अथ । पथि । गमयित्वा । क्लृप्तरम्योपकार्ये । कतिचित् । अवनिपालः । शर्वरीः । शर्वकल्पः । पुरम् । अविशत् । अयोध्याम् । मैथिलीदर्शनीनाम् । कुवलयितगवाक्षाम् । लोचनैः । अङ्गनानाम्
anvaya: अथ शर्वकल्पः अवनिपालः क्लृप्तरम्योपकार्ये पथि कतिचित् शर्वरीः गमयित्वा, मैथिलीदर्शनीनाम् अङ्गनानाम् लोचनैः कुवलयितगवाक्षाम् अयोध्याम् पुरम् अविशत् ।
meaning_english: Then, the king (Dasharatha), who was like Shiva in prowess, after spending some nights on the road in beautifully arranged camps, entered the city of Ayodhya, whose windows appeared to be filled with blue lotuses by the eyes of the women eager to see Sita.
